registry_info.name: opening_pair
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `opening` family (6 registry names, TWO value lists). One pair of rays, computed once, read on three grounds, so the family's two questions about one word stand in the same frame instead of in different rooms.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. Both value lists are PRELOADED at runtime from the members that own them (dot_product_projector + dot_aligner for `opening`, angle_sum_triangle + curvature_slider for `ground`) and checked in both directions at _ready; do not retype them here or in the script. The word `opening` is taken once and REFUSED once, on the record - see dna.declined.

opening_pair.name: Opening Pair
opening_pair.description: Two rays from one vertex, standing on a ground that can be flat, saddled or domed. `opening` is the angle the pair opens to - agreeing 40 deg, strangers 90, opposing 140, parallel 0 - and the figure is coloured by the sign of a.b in agreement_gauge's own red-grey-green. `ground` is the curvature the pair sits on, drawn twice over: as a rim-and-rib chart that barrels out on an elliptic ground and pinches in on a hyperbolic one, and as the bow of the figure's own edges, both using angle_sum_triangle's sagitta rule unaltered. Under the figure a rail runs 0-360 deg with a fixed notch at 180 and three ticks on it - the SAME pair's angle sum read on all three grounds at once, the active one a puck and the other two open pips - so every frame carries the disagreement the artifact is about. At `parallel` the two rays are one ray: no interior, nothing for the curvature to act on, and the rail goes empty rather than report a number nothing computed. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one figure per ground built once at _ready and read three ways.
interactions: read the figure against the rail
compare the three ticks: the same pair, three answers
opening_pair.qfep_connection: Two vocabularies insist they are asking the same question - what IS an angle - and disagree about where the answer lives: in the relation between two objects, or in the ground they are standing on. Holding both at once is the only way to see that the second answer contains the first. A pair does not own its opening.
opening_pair.relationships: synthesises agreement_gauge, dot_aligner, dot_product_projector and exercise_5_9_angle_between (the angle between two vectors) with angle_sum_triangle and curvature_slider (the curvature of the space); preloads two of them for the words and two more to cross-check

parameters.ground: flat | hyperbolic | elliptic - which curvature the pair is standing on (default flat)
parameters.opening: agreeing | strangers | opposing | parallel - the angle the pair opens to (default agreeing)

measurements.aabb_note: CONSTANT across all 12 variants. The panel (0.56 x 0.65 x 0.02, y 0.05-0.70) and the foot (0.56 x 0.05 x 0.10) never change, and they bound every mark: the widest thing an axis draws is the field rim on an elliptic ground, which bulges to x = +-(0.21 + 0.0252) = +-0.2352 and y = 0.6752, both inside the panel. So the sweep's union box is the single-variant box and the camera does not move between tiles.

dna.axis_order_why: LAW 16. build_dna_gallery sweeps the first two axes and trims the LATER one from the tail, so `opening` is declared second and its tail is `parallel` - which is both the degenerate value and half of the predicted closest pair (opposing|parallel). A capped run therefore drops the closest pair and the degenerate row together, and keeps the default (ground=flat, opening=agreeing) and all three grounds.
dna.axis_shape: BOTH AXES ARE SIDE BY SIDE AND MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, so both must be varied and neither can be held standing - a pair has one angle and a ground has one sign. This is not asserted, it is read off the members' code. (a) dot_product_projector._apply_opening() rotates the single vector_a to ONE angle looked up in OPENING_DEGREES, and agreement_gauge._b_for_opening() returns ONE Vector3 with a single `deg` chosen by an if-chain: there is one b, so there is one angle. (b) angle_sum_triangle._bow_sign() is a `match` returning one of {+1, -1, 0} into one scalar `s`, and curvature_slider.OPENINGS maps each value to one float K: there is one polyline, so there is one sign. Neither axis NESTS - no value contains another - so trimming a tail loses a case rather than lowering a ceiling. The SIMULTANEITY the family cannot show lives in the cross itself and in the rail, which carries all three grounds' readings of whatever pair is on screen, at every value.
dna.default:
ground=flat, opening=agreeing. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS (law 15), so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the preservation rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of PLACED artifacts and has no work to do here. It was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the safest.

WHY flat AND NOT elliptic. `flat` is the default of BOTH members that own the word (angle_sum_triangle and curvature_slider) and it is the one value where the artifact can be caught making a claim that is exactly, checkably true: the figure is three straight chords and the measured angle sum is 180.000000000 deg at agreeing, at strangers AND at opposing - three differently-shaped triangles, one answer. That invariance IS the parallel postulate, and it is what the other two grounds are a departure FROM. A visitor who meets only the default meets the theorem; the two curvatures are one token away.

WHY agreeing AND NOT strangers. `strangers` is the loudest single frame - cos theta is exactly zero, the figure goes grey, the family's whole punchline - and it is the wrong default for the same reason `made` was wrong for taxonomy_hall: it is the special case. `agreeing` at 40 deg is the generic case, positive and unremarkable, which is where the family's four members all actually ship (40, 35.5, 60 and ~16 deg) and the only opening from which all three of the others read as a departure.
dna.was: did not exist, and nothing shipped was touched. This is the cross-member argument the six `opening` declarations leave unbuilt. The corpus carries ONE axis word with TWO value lists that never meet: agreeing|strangers|opposing|parallel across agreement_gauge, dot_aligner, dot_product_projector and exercise_5_9_angle_between, and flat|hyperbolic|elliptic across angle_sum_triangle and curvature_slider. Both promotions noticed the collision in 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-05 and both wrote the same sentence into their notes - that the value lists tell the two senses apart - and then each stood in its own list and could not reach the other. angle_sum_triangle can draw the theorem failing but has no pair to fail it ON; agreement_gauge can open a pair to any of four cases but only ever on a plane.
dna.shared_with:
`opening` is dot_product_projector.OPENINGS verbatim, in order, which is agreement_gauge's list in agreement_gauge's order, seconded by dot_aligner and exercise_5_9_angle_between. It is PRELOADED at runtime from dot_product_projector.gd AND cross-checked against dot_aligner.gd, in both directions, with push_error on any divergence. The three named angles come from dot_product_projector.OPENING_DEGREES (strangers 90, opposing 140, parallel 0) rather than being retyped. `agreeing` is in NO member's angle table, because every member short-circuits it to its own shipped pose - 40 deg (agreement_gauge), 35.5 (dot_product_projector), 60 (exercise_5_9_angle_between), ~16 (dot_aligner). A synthesis has no shipped pose to hand back, so it takes the number of the artifact that OWNS the word: 40.0. That is a choice and it is on the record.

`ground`'s VALUES are angle_sum_triangle.OPENING_VALUES verbatim, in that artifact's order, preloaded and cross-checked as a SET against curvature_slider.OPENINGS - a set and not a list because that member stores the three values as a Dictionary keyed in K order (hyperbolic, flat, elliptic) rather than in declaration order. The arithmetic is shared too, not just the words: SAGITTA_RATIO (0.06) and ARC_SEGMENTS (14) are read out of angle_sum_triangle.gd and its bow formula - bulge = 4t(1-t) * s * chord, laid along (mid - centroid) - is reproduced formula for formula. The ratio is a fraction of the chord and therefore dimensionless, so it transplants to this figure's scale untouched, which is exactly why it is read and not re-tuned.

agreement_gauge is list (a)'s ORIGINAL owner and is deliberately NOT preloaded: it extends a scene base and preloads three .tscn interactables, and a synthesis should not drag a control-panel rig into a still. dot_product_projector carries the identical list character for character in a zero-preload `extends Node3D` file AND carries the angle table agreement_gauge keeps as a local if-chain. Its three rail colours (COLOR_RED, COLOR_GREY, COLOR_GREEN) and its red-grey-green mapping of cos(theta) ARE transcribed rather than preloaded, for that reason; they are three Color literals no gate can check, and this sentence is the record.
dna.declined:
THE WORD `opening` FOR THE SECOND AXIS - refused, and the refusal is the finding. Both halves of the family call their axis `opening`, and this is the one artifact that holds both. It cannot call both of them that: a registry dna.axes block is a dict and cannot hold the key twice, and one script cannot hold two @export vars of one name. So the curvature axis is called `ground` and keeps angle_sum_triangle's three answers unaltered. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary (folding_past); taking the ANSWERS and declining the word, when the word is already spoken for inside the same object, is the honest half. The collision was survivable for six years of members precisely because no member ever had to hold both senses at once - which is the argument for building this artifact, and the reason the refusal had to happen here rather than anywhere else.

ALSO DECLINED: a third axis over what the rail reports (cosine | projection | angle, agreement_gauge's `measure`). It is a real axis and it is visible in a still, but it would put a second reading on the same rail that already carries three grounds, and a rail with two meanings cannot be read at a glance. One axis measured cleanly beats two with a seam in them.
dna.framing_why:
Derived from the UNION AABB across every value of every axis, which here is also the single-variant AABB because the panel and the foot bound every mark at all twelve cells (see measurements.aabb_note). size = (0.56, 0.70, 0.10); diagonal = sqrt(0.3136 + 0.4900 + 0.0100) = 0.90200 m; radius = 0.45100. dist = 0.45100 / tan(17 deg) * 1.9 * 0.55 = 1.47516 * 1.045 = 1.54154 m, so the visible frame is 2 * 1.9 * 0.45100 * 0.55 = 0.94259 m across and the sweep resolves 760 / 0.94259 = 806.3 px/m.

WHY BELOW 1.0. The subject is a WIDE FLAT PANEL and the camera fits by DIAGONAL, so framing 1.0 would put a 0.70 m body in a 1.714 m frame. At the 35.5 deg yaw the panel's 0.56 m width projects to 0.456 m and its 0.70 m height to 0.676 m, which at framing 1.0 is 27% x 39% of frame - the shape of a correctly-framed picture of nothing. At 0.55 it is 48% x 72%, and the rasterised subject share is 39.0% of the frame with a bbox of 406 x 632 px. The box is FULL rather than airy (it is a solid slab), so unlike taxonomy_hall this share can be read straight (law 10).

EVERY MARK GAUGED AT THAT SCALE (law 4), foreshortened by cos(0.62) = 0.814 in x and cos(0.26) = 0.966 in y: figure edge 12 mm -> 7.9 x 9.3 px; field rim 9 mm -> 5.9 x 7.0; field rib 7 mm -> 4.6 x 5.5; rail body 16 mm tall -> 12.5 px; the 180 notch 9 x 44 mm -> 5.9 x 34 px; a ground pip 9 x 22 mm -> 5.9 x 17; the active puck 18 x 30 mm -> 11.8 x 23; a bead 20 mm -> 13.1 x 15.6; caption glyphs at font_size 15 / pixel_size 0.0012 -> 18 mm -> 14.5 px. Nothing this artifact draws is under 4.6 px. The marks are flat RIBBONS with real width rather than ImmediateMesh line strips, which render one pixel wide whatever the camera does - the reason angle_sum_triangle's own figure is hard to read on a tile.
dna.z_stack: LAW 7, written out before the capture. Front to back: caption glyphs +0.032; caption plate +0.030 (constant); beads +0.028; the figure's edges +0.024; the FIXED 180 notch +0.020; the active ground's puck +0.018; the other two grounds' pips +0.016; rail body +0.012 (constant); field ribs +0.010; field rim +0.008; slate panel -0.020 to 0.000; foot -0.070 to +0.030. Every mark either axis draws is IN FRONT of every constant piece of furniture, and no layer is a slab spanning another's interval - the panel is 20 mm thick and sits ENTIRELY BEHIND z = 0 while the deepest mark is at +8 mm. Screen-x extents: everything lives inside x = +-0.28 and the two mark groups are separated in y (field 0.23-0.65, rail 0.148-0.192, caption 0.055-0.121) with the same z to within 12 mm, so the separations survive projection. The one body that protrudes forward is the foot (+0.030), and it tops out at y = 0.05 while the lowest mark starts at y = 0.055; the camera pitches DOWN 15 deg, so a nearer, lower body cannot rise over a farther, higher one. Verified in the rasteriser: the caption plate, the rail and all three ticks are visible in all 12 frames.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency (crop to the union subject bbox, neutralise each frame's own corner background, greyscale, resize 160x160, mean of the hottest 5% of |a-b|), by rasterising all 12 variants at the sweep's exact camera - RES 760, FOV 34, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, PAD 1.9, dist = radius/tan(FOV/2)*PAD*0.55.

CLOSEST PAIR: `opening` = opposing | parallel, in the context ground=hyperbolic. PREDICTED 17.71% focus (0.89% frame).

THE ARITHMETIC. These are the two openings that put the least ink on the panel, so the union of changed pixels is smallest and the hottest 5% of the crop is diluted by everything that did not move. At opposing the triangle is at its flattest - base |Ta - Tb| = 2 * 0.175 * sin(70 deg) = 0.329 m against a height of 0.175 * cos(70 deg) = 0.0599 m, an aspect of 5.5:1 - and on a hyperbolic ground the long top edge bows INWARD by 4(0.25)(0.06)(0.329) = 0.0197 m, which lands its midpoint at y = 0.4153, i.e. exactly on the centroid, collapsing the figure toward a single horizontal stroke. At parallel the figure IS a single stroke, 0.175 m long. Two thin strokes differ over a smaller area than any two open triangles do, and the frame numbers agree: 0.89% here against 1.37% for agreeing|strangers.

RUNNER-UP: opposing | parallel at ground=flat, 18.89%, and agreeing | parallel at ground=hyperbolic, 18.24%. Every pair involving `parallel` is quieter than every pair that does not, in all three ground contexts - see dna.relationship.

THE `ground` AXIS'S OWN CLOSEST PAIR is flat | hyperbolic at opening=parallel, 38.13%, which is more than double the opening axis's closest. Both axes clear WEAK_FOCUS (12%) by a wide margin in a flat rasteriser.

THIS NUMBER IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST (law 13). Measured across the corpus, every prediction has under-shot by 1.5x to 6.7x, because a Python rasteriser has one light, flat shading and no shadows, ambient occlusion or antialiasing. TWO CAVEATS SPECIFIC TO THIS ARTIFACT, in opposite directions: (i) the factor should be SMALLER here than the corpus average, because every mark an axis draws is an UNSHADED flat ribbon in one plane - the raster models those almost completely, and the only shaded bodies (panel, foot) are identical in all twelve frames; (ii) the caption's GLYPHS are not modelled at all, only its plate, and the caption text changes at every one of the twelve cells, so that signal is missing from the prediction entirely. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 17.71% ON THE CLOSEST PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE: the only artifact in the corpus ever to land under its own prediction (operations_gallery, 0.09% against 4.18%) was rendering nothing.
dna.relationship:
A TESTABLE CLAIM ABOUT THE TWO AXES TOGETHER, not just a number (law 20). At opening=parallel the two rays are ONE ray: no interior, no bow direction, no area for the curvature to act on. So at that value the figure is drawn IDENTICALLY on all three grounds (the same two points, no bow, the same colour) and the rail carries no ticks at all. Everything that separates the three grounds at parallel is therefore the FIELD CHART ALONE - the rim and four ribs behind the figure.

CLAIM 1 (ordering, 3 columns x 4 values): for each of the three ground pairs, `parallel` is the STRICT MINIMUM across the four openings. Predicted: flat|hyperbolic reads 42.43 / 42.22 / 39.52 / 38.13 at agreeing / strangers / opposing / parallel; flat|elliptic 42.61 / 42.44 / 40.00 / 38.77; hyperbolic|elliptic 45.97 / 44.12 / 40.56 / 39.46. The margins are thin - 1.39, 1.23 and 1.10 points - so this is a claim that can lose. FALSIFIER: if parallel is not the minimum in all three columns, the reading is that the field chart dominates the ground axis so completely that the figure's contribution is under the render's own noise.

CLAIM 2 (decomposition, and the number to be wrong about): subtracting the parallel column from the agreeing column, the FIELD CHART accounts for 38.13/42.43 = 89.9%, 38.77/42.61 = 91.0% and 39.46/45.97 = 85.8% of the ground axis's hottest-5% signal, leaving 10.1%, 9.0% and 14.2% to the figure's bow and the rail's puck. If the sweep puts the figure's share above 30%, the field chart is drawn far weaker in a real render than in a flat raster and the ribs should be widened.

CLAIM 3 (clustering, 9 comparisons x 3 contexts): the six `opening` pairs separate into two non-overlapping bands in EVERY ground context - the three pairs among {agreeing, strangers, opposing} all above 26.10%, and the three pairs involving parallel all below 22.34% - because parallel is the only value that changes the KIND of picture (it empties the rail and collapses the figure to one stroke) rather than its pose. Predicted gaps: 5.23 (flat), 4.86 (hyperbolic), 6.17 (elliptic) points, with no crossing. FALSIFIER: any crossing at all.

NOT CLAIMED, and checked before being dropped: the rank order of the six opening pairs is NOT stable across the three grounds (agreeing|opposing and strangers|opposing overtake agreeing|strangers on elliptic ground, 29.28 and 29.14 against 28.51). The two axes are not independent - `ground` bows the very edges `opening` rotates - so no equality is available here and none is asserted.
dna.findings:
THREE THINGS THE CROSS FOUND, all computed in Python before anything was built.

(1) THE FAMILY'S BOW IS NOT A CONSTANT-CURVATURE MODEL, and only a cross could show it. angle_sum_triangle's rule bows each edge by a fixed fraction of ITS OWN CHORD, so the angle excess it produces depends on the triangle's SHAPE, not only on its area. Gauss-Bonnet says the excess is K times the area, and area = (1/2)L^2 sin(theta), so agreeing (40 deg) and opposing (140 deg) have EXACTLY the same area - sin 40 = sin 140 - and must show the same excess. They do not: measured off the drawn polylines, the elliptic excess is +71.99 deg at agreeing and +49.10 deg at opposing, and excess/area comes out 7314 / 4613 / 4989 across the three openings, a 59% spread where a constant-K chart would be flat. The SIGN is always right (positive on elliptic, negative on hyperbolic, exactly zero on flat, at all four openings), so the word is not taken dishonestly - but its magnitude is a fact about a drawing convention rather than about curvature, and the rail is labelled as a MEASURED sum for that reason (law 6). Reusing the family's ratio verbatim and reporting the discrepancy was chosen over redrawing it to be faithful, which is field_room's lesson in reverse: a family's arithmetic is not this artifact's to re-tune.

(2) THE CONVENTION'S EXCESS IS EXACTLY ODD IN THE SIGN OF K. sum(hyperbolic) + sum(elliptic) = 360.000000000 deg at every opening (108.013497292 + 251.986502708, 109.357621823 + 250.642378177, 130.898649643 + 229.101350357). Tested on five random SCALENE triangles as well, where it also holds to nine decimals, so it is an identity of the bow rule and not a symmetry of this isoceles figure. It is reported rather than predicted for exactly that reason: a construction identity confirmed by a sweep is worth nothing.

(3) THE FAMILY'S BOW RULE IS DISCONTINUOUS AT ZERO AREA, and this artifact is the first object forced to meet it. angle_sum_triangle picks its bow direction as normalize(mid - centroid) and falls back to Vector3.UP when that vanishes. As theta -> 0+ the direction stays well defined and the bow magnitude does NOT shrink (it is 0.06 of the chord, and the chord does not shrink), so the limiting picture is a LENS of finite width 2 * 0.0105 m - while the truth at theta = 0 is that the two rays are one geodesic and there is nothing to bow. The limit of the convention disagrees with the object it describes. This artifact takes the object: no bow, no interior, no reading, and an empty rail. The arbitrary UP fallback is not used.
dna.still_note: WHAT A READER SHOULD NOT MISTAKE FOR A FAULT. (i) On ground=flat the rail's puck sits exactly on the 180 notch at agreeing, strangers AND opposing - three different figures, one reading. That is not a stuck indicator, it is the parallel postulate, and it is why the notch is drawn IN FRONT of the puck (z +0.020 against +0.018) and 44 mm tall against the puck's 30: the datum must stay visible when a reading lands on it. (ii) At opening=parallel the rail is EMPTY except for that notch. There is no angle to sum, and reporting 180 there would be a number nothing computed. (iii) The three ticks are close together on curved ground at agreeing and strangers (108.01 and 109.36 deg, 1.8 mm apart on the rail, about 1.5 px) because the angle sum is a fact about AREA and those two triangles have similar areas; the FIGURE tells those two openings apart, not the rail. (iv) The 40 deg and 90 deg figures point downward - the vertex is below the tips - because the bisector is fixed pointing up so the axis turns theta and nothing else. (v) At opening=opposing on ground=hyperbolic the figure does NOT read as a triangle: it reads as a narrow arrowhead whose long edge folds down through the interior and nearly meets the two side edges at the tips, where the measured corner angles are 2.6 deg. That is not a broken mesh and not a self-intersection introduced here - it is the family's fixed sagitta ratio (a fraction of the CHORD) applied faithfully to a triangle with a 5.5:1 aspect, and it is finding (1) made visible: a bow proportional to chord length is a drawing convention, not a curvature. It was left alone rather than clamped, because inventing a new bow rule to make one cell prettier would fork the vocabulary this artifact exists to hold together.
dna.standpoint: EVERY MARK LIES IN ONE PLANE FACING +Z, so this artifact is a candidate for the anamorphic check in the direction that matters least: it is legible AT the canonical standpoint (yaw 0.62 sees the panel at 35.5 deg off normal, foreshortening the width to 81%) and would go edge-on and unreadable near yaw 1.57. If either axis ever reads INERT here, that verdict would be about the standpoint being wrong for a flat subject, not about the axis - run tools/probe_anamorphic.py before believing it. No such verdict is expected: the predicted floor is 17.71% on the closest pair of either axis.
dna.verification: python tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=opening_pair. Godot was NOT run (law 19); all geometry, framing and pixel predictions are Python arithmetic against the sweep's own camera constants, and the rasteriser and the .gd share every constant by construction (the rasteriser parses SAGITTA_RATIO, ARC_SEGMENTS, OPENINGS and OPENING_DEGREES out of the same two member scripts the .gd preloads).
